# Judges Chapter 15 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), c. 1008 CE | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/JDG_page_284.jpg, JDG_page_285.jpg

### Samson's Revenge

1. Later on, during the wheat harvest, Samson took a young goat as a gift and went to visit his wife. "I'm going into my wife's room," he told her father. But her father wouldn't let him in.

2. "I assumed you must totally hate her," her father explained, "so I gave her in marriage to your best man. But look, her younger sister is even more beautiful. Why not take her instead?"

3. Samson said, "This time I can't be blamed for everything I'm about to do to you Philistines."

4. Then Samson went out and caught 300 foxes. He tied their tails together in pairs, and he fastened a torch to each pair of tails.

5. Then he lit the torches and let the foxes run through the grain fields of the Philistines. He burned all their grain to the ground, including the sheaves and the standing grain, as well as their vineyards and olive groves.

6. "Who did this?" the Philistines demanded. "Samson," was the reply, "because his father-in-law from Timnah gave Samson's wife to be the wife of his best man." So the Philistines went and burned her and her father to death.

7. "Because you did this," Samson vowed, "I won't rest until I've taken my revenge on you!"

8. So he attacked the Philistines with great fury and slaughtered many of them. Then he went to live in a cave in the rock of Etam.

9. The Philistines retaliated by setting up camp in Judah and spreading out near the town of Lehi.

10. The men of Judah asked, "Why are you attacking us?" The Philistines replied, "We've come to capture Samson. We've come to pay him back for what he did to us."

11. So 3,000 men of Judah went down to the cave in the rock of Etam. "Don't you realize the Philistines rule over us?" they said to Samson. "What have you done to us?" He replied, "I only did to them what they did to me."

12. "We've come to tie you up and hand you over to the Philistines," they told him. "All right," Samson said. "But promise me you won't kill me yourselves."

13. "We will only tie you up and hand you over to them," they agreed. "We won't kill you." So they tied him up with two new ropes and led him away from the rock.

14. When Samson arrived at Lehi, the Philistines came shouting in triumph. But the Spirit of the LORD came powerfully upon Samson, and the ropes on his arms snapped like charred flax, and the bindings fell off his hands.

15. He found the fresh jawbone of a donkey. He grabbed it and killed 1,000 Philistines with it.

16. Then Samson said, "With the jawbone of a donkey, I've piled them in heaps! With the jawbone of a donkey, I've killed a thousand men!"

17. When he finished his boasting, he threw the jawbone away, and that place was named Jawbone Hill.

18. Samson was now very thirsty, and he cried out to the LORD, "You have accomplished this great victory through your servant. Must I now die of thirst and fall into the hands of these pagans?"

19. So God split open a hollow in the ground at Lehi, and water gushed out. Samson drank and was revived. So he named that place "The Spring of the One Who Called Out," and it is still there at Lehi.

20. Samson judged Israel for twenty years during the period of Philistine domination.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**The escalation spiral:** Chapter 15 is a masterclass in escalating violence. Samson's wife is given away (v.2) → Samson burns the Philistine fields (v.5) → The Philistines burn his wife and father-in-law (v.6) → Samson slaughters Philistines (v.8) → The Philistines attack Judah (v.9) → Judah betrays Samson to the Philistines (v.12) → Samson kills 1,000 (v.15). Every act of revenge triggers a greater counter-revenge. No one can stop the cycle.

**Judah's betrayal (v.11):** The most devastating moment isn't the violence — it's that 3,000 men of Judah come to bind their own deliverer and hand him to the enemy. "Don't you realize the Philistines rule over us?" they say. Israel has internalized its own oppression. Samson fights the Philistines; Judah fights Samson.

— PNEUMA, AI Translator
